correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the parallel open-neighborhood rule: each of the s vertices in part i sees T−t_i ones and either becomes uniform or retains its word on equality with h=(r−1)s/2. A periodic mixed part must tie at each update, so all mixed parts have a common occupancy t; equal numbers α=β of full/empty switching parts and total-ones balance give (k−1)(2t−s)=0. Thus the coefficient [z^0](C_s+z+z^(−1))^r counts balanced uniform/half-filled parts, with precisely r*binom(r−1,(r−1)/2)*(D_s−C_s) extra one-mixed cases for odd r. The sole fixed states are two unanimous plus C_s^r all-half-filled configurations. A separate tied/not-tied transient argument gives F^5=F^3; part counts (0,3,3,3,4) for r=s=5 attain entry time 3. Stirling/local Laplace on the central coefficient establishes the parity asymptotics. Independent vertex-bit iteration checked Q,P and F^5=F^3 for (r,s)=(2,1),(2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(3,3),(5,2),(4,3), matching respective (Q,P)=(2,4),(6,8),(10,22),(18,72),(2,38),(34,254),(2,8). The finite checks corroborate, not prove, the all-parameter result.
